verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Steam rising from the kettle—
this morning too
I forget to call anyone back.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The neighbor's cat sits on the fence again,
patient as a clock
that no one winds anymore.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust collects on the piano lid—
I still remember
which keys were always out of tune.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone left the porch light burning all night—
by morning
even the moths had given up on it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
A crack in the sidewalk
holds one yellow leaf—
today I'll take the long way home.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain fills the empty birdbath—
no birds have come by
since the neighbors took their feeder down.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The bus arrives early for once—
I let it go
and stand here a little longer.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's wind chimes, out of tune—
still, I pause
to hear what the breeze is saying.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
My phone buzzes with someone else's news—
I put it face down
and watch the streetlight flicker on

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A cat crosses the yard, unbothered—
I envy the way
it owns every step it takes.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off in the other room—
I stay on the porch
counting how many stars still bother.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone's laundry snaps on the line—
I forget for a moment
which shirt used to be mine.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The neighbor's dog quits barking mid-howl—
silence takes the yard
like it was only borrowed.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Streetlight flickers on early—
I keep walking
like the dark hasn't noticed yet.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The bus pulls away half-empty—
I wave anyway
at no one I recognize.
